summary: GCP service account impersonation failing for Private deployment using Workload Identity Pool - 403 on token exchange
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Nimbus Health) reports that calls from their Private deployment to external GCP resources intermittently return 403 during Redwood's token-exchange step. The failing code-path is Redwood's internal service-account impersonation flow used when Private is configured to obtain short-lived credentials via GCP Workload Identity Federation.

Impact:
- Customer unable to perform model fetches and data-sync jobs from GCS; observed errors persist across multiple hosts in their Private cluster.
- Intermittent but frequent affecting production traffic for selected tenants.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (v2026.02.3) deployed to customer-managed GCP project (prod, us-central1).
- Workload Identity Pool configured with external OIDC provider from customer's IdP.

Observed behavior:
- Redwood logs show 403 error during STS exchange: 'Caller does not have permission to impersonate service account' and GCP Audit logs show principalDoesNotHavePermission for iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken.
- API requests to /v1/models/fetch return 403 with minimal error text; customer sees 'permission denied' in their app.

Expected behavior:
- Redwood should successfully exchange the incoming subject token for a short-lived GCP access token and proceed with the GCS/model fetch.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure Redwood Private with Workload Identity federation and map incoming external subject to target service account (customer-sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com).
2) Trigger model fetch or GCS access from Private runtime.
3) Observe token-exchange failures and 403 responses in Redwood agent logs.

Logs / errors (excerpt):
- azurelike-redwood-agent[1234]: sts: exchange failed: google: APICallError: 403 'Request had insufficient authentication scopes.'
- GCP Audit log: principalDoesNotHavePermission: principals/123456789095 does not have iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken on serviceAccount:customer-sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
steps_to_reproduce: See 'Steps to reproduce' section in description. Reproducible when Workload Identity mapping is present and the impersonator principal lacks roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Workload Identity subject mapping was correct but the impersonating principal (the one Redwood uses to call IAM Credentials API) lacked the required role. Customer IAM bindings showed a custom binding that granted iam.serviceAccountUser but not iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator. Verified with 'gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy' and replayed token exchange with 'gcloud iam service-accounts signJwt' which returned PERMISSION_DENIED.

We also observed that when the customer temporarily granted roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to the impersonator principal, token exchange succeeded and model fetch completed. No code changes required on Redwood side.

Root cause: missing roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the impersonator/service-account used for token generation in customer's GCP IAM policy. The error surfaced as a 403 at the Redwood token-exchange layer and propagated to the customer's requests.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Priya Rao (Support): Logged initial report and requested IAM policy export and GCP audit logs from customer.

2026-03-10 12:04 - Customer (N. Gupta): Provided 'gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy' output and audit logs. Policy showed binding to roles/iam.serviceAccountUser but not roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator.

2026-03-10 15:30 - Alex Kim (SRE): Reproduced error in staging by removing iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator; confirmed identical audit log entries. Suggested temporary fix to add role and asked customer to grant it to impersonator principal.
2026-03-11 08:22 - Customer: Applied role binding roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to the impersonator principal. Reported that model fetches resumed successfully and errors ceased.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Alex Kim: Verified customer's production logs and confirmed no further 403s in the token-exchange path since 2026-03-11 08:20 UTC. Requested closure and documented remediation steps.
2026-03-12 10:20 - Priya Rao: Customer acknowledged resolution and asked for guidance to automate IAM checks; provided runbook link.
resolution: Applied recommended remediation: customer granted roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to the impersonator principal (service account used by Redwood Private for token exchange). Verified successful token exchanges and model fetches. Provided a short runbook to customer for Workload Identity checks and created an internal follow-up task to add an automated IAM sanity-check in the Private onboarding flow.
follow_up_actions:
1) Create an automated IAM check that validates presence of roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator and roles/iam.serviceAccountUser for configured impersonation principals.
2) Update Private onboarding docs to explicitly list required roles and a sample 'gcloud' snippet.
3) Add clearer error text in the token-exchange layer to surface 'missing iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator' in 403 responses.
